ruleset.name: jpinpoint-kotlin-concurrent-rules
ruleset.description: jPinpoint rule set for performance aware Kotlin coding related to concurrency, sponsored by Rabobank.

rule.name: AvoidCompletionServiceTake
rule.description: Problem: take() stalls indefinitely in case of hanging threads and consumes a thread. Solution: use poll() with a timeout value and handle the timeout. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidFutureGetWithoutTimeout
rule.description: Problem: Stalls indefinitely in case of hanging threads and consumes a thread. Solution: Provide a timeout value and handle the timeout. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidFutureJoinWithoutTimeout
rule.description: Problem: Stalls indefinitely in case of hanging thread(s) and consumes a thread. Solution: Provide a timeout before the join and handle the timeout. For example a future.get(timeout, unit), an orTimeout() or a completeOnTimeout(). You may want to use CompletableFuture.allOf() too. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidUnguardedAssignmentToNonFinalFieldsInSharedObjects
rule.message: Avoid unguarded assignments to non-final fields in objects shared among threads. Access thread-safely AND use @GuardedBy.
rule.description: Problem: Multiple threads typically access fields of a singleton or may access fields in session scoped objects. Unguarded assignment to a non-final (var) field is thread-unsafe and may cause corruption or visibility problems. It may also unintentionally mix-up session data. Solution: Make the properties val and unmodifiable. If they really need to be mutable, make access thread-safe: use @Synchronized and @GuardedBy or @Volatile. Notes 1. For autowiring/injection, the assignment of the reference is thread safe, so var is acceptable. The unmodifiable/thread-safe requirement for that field still holds. Also make sure no other thread-unsafe assignment is made to that field. 2. In case you are sure the Component is used in single threaded context only (e.g. a Tasklet), annotate the class with @NotThreadSafe to make this explicit. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidNonPrivateFieldsInSharedObjects
rule.message: Avoid non-private properties in shared objects. Make properties private to ensure thread-safety.
rule.description: Problem: A singleton, or more general: an object shared among threads, has a property that is not private. These properties can possibly be modified from other classes. Solution: Make the properties private. Note: properties are excluded when annotated with: @Autowired/@Value/@Inject. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidCommonPoolForFutureAsync
rule.message: Avoid using the common thread pool for future.supplyAsync, use a separate pool.
rule.description: Problem: CompletableFuture.supplyAsync is typically used for remote calls. By default, it uses the common pool. The number of threads in the common pool is equal to the number of CPUs, which is suitable for in-memory processing. For I/O, however, this number is typically not suitable because most time is spent waiting for the response and not in CPU. The common pool must not be used for blocking calls. Solution: A separate, properly sized, pool of threads (an Executor) should be used for the async calls. (jpinpoint-rules)
